mainTopic: Is the child of a גוי or an עבד with a בת ישראל a ממזר, כשר, or only פגום for כהונה?
overview: The גמרא asks whether a child born to a Jewish woman from a גוי or an עבד is a ממזר. First it tries to explain who "הכל מודים" includes. A ברייתא knocks down the first answer, so רב יוסף says it includes רבי, quoting רב דימי's report that רבי calls the child a ממזר. רבי אמי rules the same way in a real case, citing רבי יוחנן, רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא. רב יוסף answers that counting names proves nothing, since רב, שמואל, רבי יהושע בן לוי and others call the child כשר. The lenient Sages still agree the child is פגום for כהונה, which the גמרא proves with a קל וחומר from an אלמנה and a פסוק. אביי then points to רבין's report that רבי is lenient. רב, רב מתנה, רב יהודה and רבא all treat the child as כשר, and the story of רב refusing his daughter does not change his ruling. רבה adds that the child of a half-slave is surely כשר, and רב יוסף begins a statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why even the strict view would agree about a gentile or a slave
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the first explanation of "הכל מודים". The view that a ממזר comes only from relations punishable by כרת is limited to ordinary לאו prohibitions, where קידושין still take effect. With a גוי or an עבד, קידושין do not take effect at all, so the case is treated like חייבי כריתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule (no ממזר from a לאו) applies only to people who are forbidden by a לאו, where קידושין still take effect. But here, with a גוי or an עבד, קידושין do not take effect, so it is treated like relations punishable by כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its first answer to "who is included in הכל מודים". It explains why even the view that a ממזר comes only from כרת relations would agree that a child of a גוי or an עבד is a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key test is whether קידושין can take effect. With ordinary לאו prohibitions they can, so the strict view says the child is not a ממזר. With a גוי or an עבד they cannot, which makes the case like חייבי כריתות, so the child would be a ממזר even according to that view.

keyTerms.meaning: Relations forbidden by a negative commandment (a לאו), not punished by כרת
Betrothal takes effect with them
Relations punishable by כרת (spiritual cutting off)
A non-Jew and a (non-Jewish) slave

steps.confusionAlert: This step is the end of an answer that began before this section. It is not a brand-new statement. The גמרא is still explaining who "הכל מודים" includes.

phrases.english: to those forbidden by a negative prohibition, with whom betrothal takes effect,
but here, a gentile and a slave,
since betrothal does not take effect with them —
it is like those liable for karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אבל הכא גוי ועבד כיון דלא תפסי בהו קידושין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first answer to "מאן הכל מודים", which began before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even the view requiring כרת for ממזרות agrees, because the lack of קידושין makes the case like חייבי כריתות.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the strict view disagrees
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a dispute. The תנא קמא says a child of a גוי or an עבד with a Jewish woman is a ממזר. רבי שמעון בן יהודה disagrees: a ממזר comes only from an ערוה punishable by כרת. So the person who holds the strict view does not agree after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A גוי or an עבד who has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר. רבי שמעון בן יהודה says: a ממזר comes only from someone forbidden as an ערוה and punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first answer by quoting a ברייתא. In it, רבי שמעון בן יהודה, who holds the strict כרת view, clearly disagrees about a גוי and an עבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 claimed the strict view would agree about a גוי and an עבד. Here, someone who holds that strict view is shown arguing against the first opinion, so he must hold the child is not a ממזר. That means "הכל מודים" cannot include this view.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born of certain forbidden relations, who may not marry into the general community
A forbidden sexual relationship (one of the עריות)
Punished with כרת

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: They raised an objection: a gentile or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman —
the child is a mamzer.
Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says:
There is no mamzer except from one
whose prohibition is a prohibition of forbidden relations and is punished with karet.
phrases.notes: He is arguing with the first opinion, so to him the child of a גוי or an עבד is not a ממזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the strict כרת view agrees about a גוי and an עבד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון בן יהודה holds the strict כרת view and still disputes the ruling that the child is a ממזר, so not "everyone" agrees.

steps.title: רב יוסף: "Everyone" includes רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a new answer. "הכל מודים" is meant to include רבי. Even though רבי rejects רבי עקיבא's strict view that a חלוצה is like an ערוה, he still agrees that the child of a גוי or an עבד is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: Who is "everyone agrees" coming to include? רבי. Even though רבי says that a certain rule was said only according to רבי עקיבא, who treated a חלוצה like an ערוה, and רבי himself does not hold that way, about a גוי and an עבד he agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first answer fell, רב יוסף offers a new identification of who "הכל מודים" is coming to include: רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think רבי is lenient about ממזרות, since he does not treat a חלוצה like an ערוה the way רבי עקיבא does. "הכל מודים" teaches that even so, for a גוי or an עבד, רבי agrees the child is a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the earlier answer for a new one)
Everyone agrees
A woman released from יבום through חליצה
He does not hold this view
He agrees

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Who is meant by 'all agree'? Rabbi,
phrases.notes: רבי here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: even though Rabbi says:
these words were not said
phrases.notes: This refers to a later משנה about a יבם who betroths the woman after he already did חליצה with her.

phrases.english: except according to the words of Rabbi Akiva,
who would treat a woman released by chalitza like a forbidden relative,
and he himself does not hold that way,
regarding a gentile and a slave, he agrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in Step 2 with a new identification.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-identifying who the phrase "הכל מודים" is coming to include.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Everyone" was meant to include the strict view that a ממזר comes only from כרת relations.
steps.terutzMaskana: "Everyone" includes רבי, who is lenient about a חלוצה but agrees about a גוי and an עבד.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the phrase "הכל מודים" is chosen to include a specific authority who might have been expected to disagree.

steps.title: Proof that רבי holds the child is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף backs up his claim. רב דימי reported, through רב יצחק בר אבודימי, that "our teacher" (רבי) ruled that a child of a גוי or an עבד with a Jewish woman is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: For when רב דימי came, he said that רב יצחק בר אבודימי said in the name of our teacher: A גוי or an עבד who has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that רבי really does rule this way, which supports רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 claimed רבי agrees about a גוי and an עבד. This report quotes רבי directly ruling that the child is a ממזר, so the claim is confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to Bavel)
In the name of
Our teacher, a title for רבי יהודה הנשיא

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף: "הכל מודים" includes רבי. Even though רבי does not treat a חלוצה like an ערוה, he holds that the child of a גוי or an עבד with a Jewish woman is a ממזר.

phrases.english: For when Rav Dimi came,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Avudimi said in the name of our teacher:
phrases.notes: "Our teacher" is רבי, the same רבי from the step before.

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: a gentile or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman —
the child is a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 3's claim about רבי's view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי agrees the child of a גוי or an עבד is a ממזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב דימי's report from רב יצחק בר אבודימי in רבי's name.

steps.title: A real case: a redeemed captive pregnant from a gentile
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא and רבי תנחום redeemed captive women who came to טבריה. One was pregnant from a גוי, so they came to רבי אמי to ask about the child's status.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא, the officer of the capital, and רבי תנחום the son of רבי חייא, from the village of עכו, redeemed some captive women who came from ארמון to טבריה. One of them was pregnant from a גוי, and they came before רבי אמי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a related story that sets up a practical question for רבי אמי. The ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story shows the question was not only theoretical. A real child was about to be born, and its status had to be decided.

keyTerms.meaning: They redeemed
Captive women
She became pregnant
Before him (to ask a question)

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha, the officer of the capital,
and Rabbi Tanchum son of Rabbi Chiya,
the man of the village of Akko,
redeemed certain captive women
who came from Armon to Tiberias.
There was one who had become pregnant from a gentile,
and they came before Rabbi Ami,

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אחא שר הבירה ורבי תנחום בריה דרבי חייא איש כפר עכו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a practical case on the same topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the status of a child born to a Jewish woman from a גוי?

steps.title: רבי אמי: Three great אמוראים say the child is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answered by quoting רבי יוחנן, רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא, who all say that a child of a גוי or an עבד with a Jewish woman is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: רבי יוחנן, רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא are the ones who say: A גוי or an עבד who has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי rules on the captive's case by citing three major authorities who say the child is a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי does not give his own reasoning. He relies on the weight of רבי יוחנן, רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא. So in this story the practical ruling follows the view that the child is a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Who say

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי ruled, based on רבי יוחנן, רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא, that the child of a גוי and a Jewish woman is a ממזר. רב יוסף rejects this way of proving it in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: He said to them: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar
and Rabbi Chanina are the ones who say:
phrases.notes: He is telling them to follow these three, so the baby will be a ממזר.

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: a gentile or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman —
the child is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר להו רבי יוחנן ורבי אלעזר ורבי חנינא דאמרי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the practical question raised in Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The child is a ממזר, following רבי יוחנן, רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the view that the child is a ממזר being applied as an actual ruling, not only discussed in theory.

steps.title: Counting famous names proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects רבי אמי's proof from three big names. Just as many great אמוראים say the child is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Is it such a big deal to count men? Look, רב and שמואל in בבל, and רבי יהושע בן לוי and בר קפרא in ארץ ישראל (some say: take out בר קפרא and put in the זקני דרום) all say that when a גוי or an עבד lives with a Jewish woman, the child is כשר!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף says you cannot decide the הלכה just by listing big names. There is an equally impressive list on the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רבי אמי quoted three great Sages who say the child is a ממזר. רב יוסף answers that four great Sages say the child is כשר. So counting heads cannot settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: A big deal, something impressive
To count men, listing who holds an opinion
The elders of the South, a group of Sages
Fit, with no flaw in lineage; may marry into the community

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Is it a big deal to count men?!
phrases.notes: He means: just listing names, like רבי אמי did, doesn't prove anything.

phrases.english: Look, Rav and Shmuel in Babylonia,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי וּבַר קַפָּרָא בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi and bar Kappara in Eretz Yisrael,
and some say: take out bar Kappara
and put in the Elders of the South,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרִי: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: who say: a gentile or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman,
the child is fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אמי's answer, which relied on a list of names.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The method of proving the הלכה by counting Sages.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An equal or larger list of great אמוראים holds the opposite view, that the child is כשר.

steps.title: רב יוסף rules like רבי
steps.stepSummary: Instead of counting names, רב יוסף bases the ruling on רבי, who says the child is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: This is the view of רבי. When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יצחק בר אבודימי: They said in the name of our teacher: a גוי or an עבד who lives with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives his real basis for the strict ruling: it is the view of רבי, not a count of names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the report from step 4, but now it does a new job. Since the names on each side cancel out, what decides the matter is that רבי himself holds the child is a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Our teacher, meaning רבי יהודה הנשיא
A child of a forbidden union who may not marry into the regular community
When he came, from ארץ ישראל to בבל

steps.confusionAlert: This looks like a repeat of step 4. Here, though, it is used to decide the הלכה after the counting approach was rejected.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי הִיא.
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said: It is Rabbi.
For when Rav Dimi came
he said that Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avudimi said:
In the name of our teacher they said:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: A gentile or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman,
the child is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the counting proof, רב יוסף gives the real reason: the ruling of רבי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב יוסף, the הלכה follows רבי: the child of a גוי or an עבד with a Jewish woman is a ממזר.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף does not decide by counting Sages. He rules that the child is a ממזר because רב דימי reported that this is רבי's view. אביי challenges this report in step 16.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: the child is spoiled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a middle-ground description: the child is מקולקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says: The child is spoiled.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement from רבי יהושע בן לוי says the child is 'spoiled'. This sets up the גמרא's next question about what that word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is unclear, because רבי יהושע בן לוי was just listed among those who say the child is כשר. The word 'מקולקל' must mean some smaller flaw, and the גמרא will figure out which one.

keyTerms.meaning: Spoiled, damaged; having some flaw in lineage

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
The child is spoiled.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אוֹמֵר: הַוָּלָד מְקוּלְקָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a statement from one of the Sages listed in step 7, which seems to describe a flaw.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The child of a גוי or an עבד with a Jewish woman is מקולקל.

steps.title: Spoiled for whom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'spoiled' refers to. It cannot mean marrying into the קהל, since רבי יהושע בן לוי said the child is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Spoiled for whom? If you say for marrying into the community, didn't רבי יהושע say the child is כשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of flaw 'spoiled' means. It rules out the first guess, because it would contradict what רבי יהושע בן לוי said earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'spoiled' meant the child cannot marry a regular Jew, that would make the child like a ממזר. But רבי יהושע בן לוי was quoted in step 7 as saying the child is כשר, so it must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: For whom? In regard to what?
If you say, introducing a possible answer to test it
The community of Israel, meaning permission to marry a regular Jew

phrases.english: For whom?
If you say for the community,
but Rabbi Yehoshua said:
phrases.notes: This is the same רבי יהושע בן לוי, quoted in step 7's list.

phrases.english: the child is fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the word 'מקולקל' in step 9 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly the child is disqualified from, according to רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: Spoiled means unfit for כהונה
steps.stepSummary: 'Spoiled' means the child is unfit for כהונה. All the אמוראים who call the child כשר agree to this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means for כהונה. All the אמוראים who say the child is כשר agree that the child is flawed for כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'spoiled' means the child cannot marry into a כהן family. This is a smaller flaw that even the lenient Sages accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is no contradiction. The child may marry a regular Jew (כשר for the קהל) but is פגום for כהונה. All the lenient אמוראים in step 7 agree to this.

keyTerms.meaning: The priesthood; marrying into a כהן family
Blemished, flawed in lineage
Who declare it fit, the lenient view

steps.whatToRemember: The lenient view says the child is כשר to marry into the קהל but פגום for כהונה.

phrases.english: Rather, for the priesthood,
for all the amoraim who declare him fit
agree that the child is flawed for the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מקולקל means פגום לכהונה, and all the lenient אמוראים agree to this.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from an אלמנה
steps.stepSummary: The flaw for כהונה is proven by a קל וחומר from an אלמנה married to a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes from a קל וחומר from an אלמנה. An אלמנה with a כהן גדול is forbidden only to some people, yet her child is flawed. This woman is forbidden to everyone, so surely her child is flawed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the child is פגום for כהונה, using a קל וחומר from a known case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אלמנה is forbidden only to a כהן גדול, yet her child from him is פגום. A Jewish woman with a גוי or an עבד is in a union forbidden to every Jew. So her child should surely be at least פגום.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
A widow, forbidden to a כהן גדול
The High Priest
Equal for everyone, a ban that applies to all Jews

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the lenient side still gives the child a flaw for כהונה. It is not just a compromise; it follows from logic.

phrases.english: From a kal vachomer from a widow:
Just as a widow with a High Priest,
whose prohibition is not the same for everyone,
her son is flawed,
this one, whose prohibition is the same for everyone,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the Jewish woman with a גוי or an עבד; no Jew may have that relationship.

phrases.english: isn't it logical that her son is flawed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 11 that the child is פגום לכהונה.
steps.raayaObject: That the child of a גוי or an עבד with a Jewish woman is פגום for כהונה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the child of an אלמנה and a כהן גדול, who is פגום.

steps.title: The widow herself becomes disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the קל וחומר: in the case of an אלמנה with a כהן גדול, the woman herself becomes a חללה, which may not be true for a גוי or עבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a widow with a כהן גדול? There, the woman herself becomes disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the קל וחומר from step 12. The source case has a feature that the new case might not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר said: if a child born from an אלמנה and a כהן גדול is unfit, then surely a child born from a forbidden union with a גוי or עבד is unfit. The challenge is that with the אלמנה, the woman herself becomes disqualified, so it makes sense that her child is too. That may not happen with a גוי or עבד.

keyTerms.meaning: "What about...?" A formula for showing the source case has a special feature, which breaks a קל וחומר
A widow married to a כהן גדול, a forbidden union
Becomes a חללה, unfit to marry a כהן

phrases.english: What about a widow with a High Priest
for there she herself becomes disqualified!
phrases.notes: She becomes a חללה. From then on she can't marry any כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר brought in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from אלמנה לכהן גדול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case has a stricter feature (the mother herself is disqualified) that may not exist with a גוי or עבד

steps.title: Here too, the woman becomes disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a גוי or עבד also disqualifies the woman as soon as they have relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, once he had relations with her, he disqualified her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The same feature exists in our case too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said the new case is weaker because the woman stays fit. The answer says she does not stay fit: relations with a גוי or עבד also make her unfit for כהונה. So the קל וחומר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, the same is true in our case
She had relations
He disqualified her

phrases.english: Here too,
once she had relations with him, he disqualified her.
phrases.notes: He means she is now unfit to marry a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the missing feature exists in the new case too
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי or עבד does not disqualify the woman, so the קל וחומר fails
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי or עבד does disqualify her, so the קל וחומר holds

steps.title: A פסוק shows a גוי or עבד disqualifies the woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון learns from the פסוק about a כהן's daughter that a גוי or עבד makes the woman unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון: From where do we know that a גוי or עבד who has relations with a כהן's daughter, a לויה, or a Jewish woman makes her unfit? Because the פסוק says, "And a כהן's daughter, when she becomes a widow or divorcee." She goes back to her father's house only if she was with a man who can make her a widow or a divorcee. A גוי or עבד is left out, because widowhood and divorce do not apply to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for its answer in step 14. The source shows that a גוי or עבד disqualifies the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lets a כהן's daughter return to eating in her father's house only after a man whose marriage can end in widowhood or divorce. A marriage with a גוי or עבד does not take effect at all. So after being with them she does not get her rights back, which means she has been made unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
A non-Jew and a non-Jewish slave
Widowhood and divorce, which only apply where a real marriage can exist
Are excluded

steps.whyThisMatters: This source proves the woman herself is disqualified. That is what saves the קל וחומר showing the child is unfit for כהונה.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
From where do we know that a gentile or a slave
who has relations with a priest's daughter
or a Levite woman or an Israelite woman
makes her unfit?
For it is stated: "And a priest's daughter
when she becomes a widow or a divorcee"

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אַלְמְנוּת וְגֵירוּשִׁין בָּהּ,
phrases.english: meaning one with whom widowhood and divorce can apply to her
This leaves out a gentile and a slave
to whom widowhood and divorce with her cannot apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 14
steps.raayaObject: That a גוי or עבד disqualifies the woman
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 22:13 as explained by רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון
steps.whatToRemember: The child is unfit for כהונה. A גוי or עבד disqualifies the woman, just like an אלמנה with a כהן גדול.

steps.title: אביי asks why to rely on רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף for basing the ruling on רב דימי's report, when he could rely on רבין's report instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What did you see that made you rely on רב דימי? Rely on רבין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב יוסף's ruling from step 8. אביי questions the report he relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף ruled the child is a ממזר because רב דימי reported that this is רבי's view. אביי says there is a different report, from רבין, that tells us something else about רבי. So why choose רב דימי's version?

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? Why did you choose this option over the other?
Rely

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: He is talking to רב יוסף.

phrases.english: What did you see
that you rely on Rav Dimi?
Rely on Ravin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the כהונה discussion to challenge רב יוסף's ruling in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reliance on רב דימי's report of רבי's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a different report of רבי's view, so choosing רב דימי needs a reason

steps.title: רבין reports that רבי is lenient
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רבי נתן and רבי יהודה הנשיא rule the child is permitted, and רבי יהודה הנשיא is רבי himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: For when רבין came, he said: רבי נתן and רבי יהודה הנשיא rule leniently on this. And who is רבי יהודה הנשיא? He is רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up אביי's challenge by quoting רבין's report. It also confirms that the person named is רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין's report says רבי holds the child is permitted. That is the opposite of רב דימי's report. Since the הלכה follows רבי, this undercuts רב יוסף's reason for calling the child a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Rule leniently, saying it is permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Both רב דימי and רבין are quoting רבי, and they quote him in opposite ways. The argument is about which report of רבי's view is correct.

phrases.english: For when Ravin came, he said:
Rabbi Natan and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi
rule leniently on this.
And who is Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi? Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the content of the report אביי says to rely on
steps.raayaObject: That רבי holds the child is permitted

steps.title: רב also ruled leniently: the story begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that רב also permits the child, and starts a story where someone asked רב about this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב also rules leniently on this. For a certain man came before רב and said to him: A גוי or עבד who has relations with a Jewish woman, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings more support for the lenient view, this time from רב. The step sets up a story, and רב's answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After rejecting רב יוסף's reliance on רב דימי, the גמרא shows the lenient view also has the backing of רב. The question to רב is laid out here, and his ruling comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules, gives a halachic ruling
Before him
What is the law?

phrases.english: And even Rav rules leniently on this.
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added by the corrected text.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב, אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: For a certain man who came before Rav said to him:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: A gentile or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further authority for the lenient view supported in step 17
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ruling given by רב in a real case (the story continues next)

steps.title: רב rules the child is כשר
steps.stepSummary: רב answers the question from step 18: the child of a גוי or עבד with a Jewish woman is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: The child is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives his answer to the man who asked him about the child of a גוי or עבד with a Jewish woman. He says the child is כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the actual proof promised in step 18 that רב permits the child. It adds רב to the list of authorities who agree with רבי, after רבין's report in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: child, offspring
fit, without a flaw in lineage, allowed to marry into a regular Jewish family

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב, a major authority, rules the child is כשר. This supports the ruling the גמרא is building toward.

phrases.english: He said to him: The child is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's answer to the question set up in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the child of a גוי or עבד with a Jewish woman is כשר.

steps.title: The man asks for רב's daughter and is refused
steps.stepSummary: The man, who was himself such a child, asks to marry רב's daughter, and רב refuses.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Give me your daughter. רב said: I will not give her to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The man who asked turns out to be such a child himself. He asks to marry רב's daughter, and רב says no. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man is testing whether רב will act on his own ruling. רב's refusal looks like it contradicts what he just said. That tension is what שימי בר חייא will point out next.

keyTerms.meaning: give me
your daughter
I will not give

phrases.english: He said to him: Give me your daughter.
phrases.notes: Now the questioner is speaking. He is himself such a child, so he asks to marry רב's daughter.

phrases.english: I will not give her to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts רב's ruling from step 19 to a personal test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב refuses to give his daughter in marriage to such a child, even though he ruled the child is כשר.

steps.title: שימי בר חייא challenges רב with the camel proverb
steps.stepSummary: רב's grandson uses a saying about a dancing camel to argue that a claim is proven only when it is tested, and רב is failing the test of his own ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: שימי בר חייא said to רב: People say, a camel in מדי dances on a tiny space the size of a קב. Well, here is the קב, here is the camel, here is מדי, and it is not dancing!
steps.whatsHappening: שימי בר חייא challenges רב. He says that if רב really believed the child is כשר, he would let this man marry his daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proverb is about big claims that fall apart when you actually check them. Everything needed for the test is here: the ruling, the man, and the daughter. Yet רב does not follow through, so it looks like he does not truly trust his own ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: people say, a common saying
camel
a קב, a small measure of volume, here meaning a tiny space
dances

steps.confusionAlert: שימי is not arguing about the law itself. He is pointing out that רב's actions do not match his ruling.

phrases.english: Shimi bar Ḥiyya said to Rav:
People say:
A camel in Medes dances on a kav.
phrases.notes: Meaning it can dance on a space just big enough to hold a kav of grain. It's an exaggerated boast.

phrases.aramaic: הָא קַבָּא, וְהָא גַּמְלָא, וְהָא מָדַי —
phrases.english: Here is the kav, and here is the camel, and here is Medes,
and it is not dancing!
phrases.notes: He means: when it comes time to act, your ruling isn't holding up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב, אָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's refusal in step 20 as inconsistent with his ruling in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's refusal to give his daughter to the man.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the child is truly כשר, refusing to marry your daughter to him shows you do not really rely on the ruling.

steps.title: רב says his refusal has nothing to do with the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that he would not give his daughter even to someone as great as יהושע בן נון, so his refusal is not about lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even if he were like יהושע בן נון, I would not give him my daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends himself. He explains that his refusal is not because of the man's lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying he would refuse even יהושע בן נון, רב shows his reason is personal. It is not a doubt about the child being כשר, so his ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: even if he were
יהושע, the student of משה, an example of a very great person
my daughter

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי נִיהְוֵי כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן —
phrases.english: He said to him: Even if he were like Joshua son of Nun,
I would not give him my daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי נִיהְוֵי כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שימי's challenge from step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating the action from the ruling: the refusal has a different reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב refuses because he doubts the child is כשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's refusal is personal and would apply even to a great man, so his ruling is not undermined.

steps.title: שימי says this man has no other options
steps.stepSummary: שימי replies that a great man refused by רב would find other wives, but this man will be refused by everyone if רב refuses him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If he were like יהושע בן נון, and you did not give him your daughter, others would give him theirs. But with this man, if you do not give him, others will not give him either.
steps.whatsHappening: שימי pushes back on רב's answer. He says the comparison to יהושע בן נון does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Refusing a great man costs him nothing, because other families will want him. But when רב refuses this man, people will assume it is because of his lineage, and nobody will marry him. So רב's refusal does act as a statement against him, even if רב did not mean it that way.

keyTerms.meaning: master, a respectful way of saying 'you'
others
they give

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הֲוָה כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן,
phrases.english: He said to him: If he were like Joshua son of Nun,

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָר לָא יָהֵיב לֵיהּ — אַחֲרִינֵי יָהֲבִי לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: if the Master would not give to him, others would give to him;

phrases.aramaic: הַאי אִי מָר לָא יָהֵיב לֵיהּ — אַחֲרִינֵי לָא יָהֲבִי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: this one, if the Master does not give to him, others will not give to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הֲוָה כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב's answer from step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison to יהושע בן נון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A great man has other options, but this man's chances depend on רב, so רב's refusal shuts every door for him.

steps.title: The man keeps pressing and dies
steps.stepSummary: The man would not leave רב alone. רב looked at him, and he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would not go away from before him. רב set his eyes on him, and he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The man keeps standing before רב and pressing him, and after רב looks at him, he dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב never changes his mind about marrying off his daughter, and he also never takes back his ruling. The main point for the סוגיא is the הלכה: רב rules the child is כשר. The personal refusal does not cancel that.

keyTerms.meaning: from before him
he set his eyes on him, a harsh look
he died

steps.whatToRemember: רב rules that the child of a גוי or עבד with a Jewish woman is כשר. His refusal to marry off his daughter was personal, and it does not change his ruling.

phrases.english: He would not go away from before him.
He set his eyes on him, and he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story that began in step 18 and led to the back-and-forth in steps 21 to 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story ends with רב's ruling that the child is כשר still in place, and his refusal staying a personal matter.

steps.title: רב מתנה and רב יהודה also rule leniently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that רב מתנה and רב יהודה also rule that the child of a non-Jew or slave and a Jewish woman is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also רב מתנה rules that such a child is permitted, and also רב יהודה rules that such a child is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more Sages, רב מתנה and רב יהודה, who rule that this child is permitted to marry into the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the story of רב, the גמרא strengthens the lenient side by adding more names. The word "also" shows that this ruling has wide support.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules, gives a halachic decision
Leniently, toward permission
And also, and even

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַב מַתְנָה מוֹרֵה בַּהּ לְהֶיתֵּירָא,
phrases.english: And also Rav Mattana rules about it leniently,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַב יְהוּדָה מוֹרֵה בַּהּ לְהֶיתֵּירָא.
phrases.english: and also Rav Yehuda rules about it leniently.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַב מַתְנָה מוֹרֵה בַּהּ לְהֶיתֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of רב, the גמרא returns to the halacha and adds more Sages who hold the lenient view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב מתנה and רב יהודה rule that the child of a non-Jew or slave and a Jewish woman is permitted.

steps.title: Proof from the advice of רב יהודה and רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה told such a man to hide his lineage or marry someone like himself. רבא told him to move away or marry someone like himself. This advice shows they held he is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: When such a man came before רב יהודה, he told him: Go hide your lineage, or marry a woman of your own kind. And when such a man came before רבא, he told him: Either move to another place, or marry a woman of your own kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the lenient rulings from real cases. Each Sage told the man how he could find a wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling him to hide his lineage or move away only makes sense if he is truly allowed to marry a regular Jewish woman. The only problem is social, because people would not want to marry him. If he were a ממזר, hiding would not help, since the marriage itself would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Hide yourself, keep your lineage hidden
Go into exile, move to a place where you are not known
A woman of your own kind, with a similar lineage
Before him

steps.confusionAlert: The Sages are not telling him to deceive anyone about something forbidden. They hold he is fully permitted, and they only want to help him avoid people's prejudice.

phrases.english: As when [such a man] came before Rav Yehuda,
he said to him: Go hide yourself,
phrases.notes: He means: keep quiet about who your father was, so families won't refuse to marry you.

phrases.english: or marry a woman of your own kind.
And when [such a man] came before Rava,
he said to him: Either go into exile,
or marry a woman of your own kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This proves the claim of step 25 that רב יהודה ruled leniently, and adds רבא as holding the same view.
steps.raayaObject: That רב יהודה, and also רבא, hold that the child of a non-Jew or slave and a Jewish woman is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Their practical advice to hide one's lineage or move away, which only makes sense if the man is permitted to marry any Jewish woman.

steps.title: The people of בי מיכסי ask about a half-slave
steps.stepSummary: The people of בי מיכסי ask רבה about the status of a child born to a Jewish woman from a man who is half slave and half free.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of בי מיכסי sent a question to רבה: A man who is half slave and half free had relations with a Jewish woman. What is the status of the child?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question comes in. What is the הלכה for the child of a man who is only half a slave?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a mixed one. The man is partly a slave and partly a free Jew. The askers want to know whether this mix creates a new problem for the child.

keyTerms.meaning: Half slave and half free, for example a slave owned by two partners where only one freed him
A Jewish woman
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי בֵּי מִיכְסֵי לְרַבָּה:
phrases.english: The people of Bei Mikhsei sent [a question] to Rabba:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
phrases.english: One who is half slave and half free
who had relations with a Jewish woman, what is [the child's status]?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי בֵּי מִיכְסֵי לְרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that the child of a full slave is permitted, the גמרא brings a question about a half-slave.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The status of a child born to a Jewish woman from a man who is half slave and half free.

steps.title: רבה: if a full slave's child is כשר, surely a half-slave's child is
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers with a קל וחומר. Since the child of a full slave is כשר, there is no question that the child of a half-slave is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Now, if about a full slave we say the child is כשר, do you even need to ask about a half-slave?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that the question is not a real question. The child of a half-slave is כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה reasons from the bigger case to the smaller one. If a man who is fully a slave does not make the child a ממזר, a man who is only half a slave certainly does not. The ruling for a full slave already covers the half-slave.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if already (opens a "how much more so" argument)
Fit, of valid lineage, permitted to marry into the Jewish people
Is it even a question?

steps.whatToRemember: The child of a full slave and a Jewish woman is כשר, so the child of a half-slave is certainly כשר as well.

phrases.english: He said to them: Now, [if about] a full slave
we say [the child] is fit,
is it a question about a half [slave]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This directly answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The child is כשר, by a קל וחומר from the case of a full slave.

steps.title: רב יוסף begins: the master of this teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף begins a statement about the Sage who is the main teacher of this הלכה. The statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The master of this teaching...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. רב יוסף starts to name the Sage who taught this הלכה, and the sentence is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא has gathered many Sages who rule leniently. Now רב יוסף begins to point to the main source of this הלכה. The full point of his words becomes clear when the sentence is finished on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The master of the teaching, the main authority behind this halacha

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: The master of the teaching
phrases.notes: "The teaching" is the rule that the child of a slave and a Jewish woman is not a ממזר. His sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returning to the main lenient ruling, רב יוסף begins to identify its chief teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet complete. רב יוסף is beginning to name the main authority behind the ruling that the child is not a ממזר.
